paragraphs.source_en: “Painting Australia Red” provided a rallying point that would get everyone excited to be part of the company and to play a role in its success. “There are lots of people who have no idea where their company is going,” asserts Jan, and consequently “they have no exciting future.” By envisioning exciting future possibilities, leaders get people to feel that they’re a part of something special. They are energized knowing that their organization is going places, and not just standing around doing what has always been done.

paragraphs.source_en: Part of enlisting others is building common ground on which everyone can stand. Equally important is the emotion that leaders express for the vision. Our research shows that in addition to expecting leaders to be forward-looking, constituents expect their leaders to be *inspiring.* People need vast reserves of energy and excitement to sustain commitment to a distant dream. Leaders are an important source of that energy. People aren’t going to follow someone who’s only mildly enthusiastic about something. People actively support those leaders who are *wildly* enthusiastic about it.
